rounds.text: Bajaj Auto is demonstrating exceptional growth and operational efficiency, with trailing twelve-month sales growing at 37% [E17] and profits surging by 55% [E21], while delivering a stellar return on equity of 29.2% [E13] and return on capital employed of 28.2% [E12]. Despite this high-velocity performance, the market under-appreciates the company's intrinsic value, which a discounted cash flow analysis places at Rs 15,928 per share [E46], representing a 23.8% margin of safety over the current market price [E47]. Furthermore, the current stock price only implies a 13.3% earnings growth rate, which is highly conservative compared to the 17.0% assumed in the base case [E48], especially given a strong sector tailwind score of +1.06 [E75] and the company's expectation to outpace industry growth in key segments [E80]. This growth is supported by strong operational milestones, such as exports surpassing 600,000 units in Q3 for the first time in 15 quarters [E91] and the EV business achieving a double-digit EBITDA margin [E90]. Conceded: the company trades at a premium P/E of 29.4x compared to the sector benchmark of 26.21x [E6], has a high P/B of 8.75x [E7], experienced a rise in borrowings to Rs 22,713 Cr [E40], and recorded a low cash conversion of 0.25x in Mar 2026 [E34].

Bajaj Auto's valuation is highly stretched, trading at a P/E of 29.4x against a sector benchmark of 26.21x [E6] and a P/B of 8.75x against a sector benchmark of 2.88x [E7]. This premium pricing is ahead of fundamentals, as 5-year price growth of 26% outpaced profit growth of 17% [E57], while institutional money flow has turned negative [E45] with foreign institutional holdings dropping from 14.37% to 9.01% [E43]. Financially, the company's quality of earnings is weak, marked by a poor cash conversion of 0.25x [E34], operating cash flow at just 46% of operating profit [E37], and a massive surge in borrowings to Rs 22,713 Cr in March 2026 from Rs 9,364 Cr a year earlier [E40]. Operational risks are also mounting due to rising cost pressures in noble and base metals [E96] and an adverse impact of INR 23,000 to INR 25,000 per electric 3-wheeler from the withdrawal of PM E-DRIVE incentives [E97]. Conceded: the company has achieved strong trailing twelve-month profit growth of 55% [E21] and boasts a high return on equity of 29.2% [E13].

Although the bear highlights premium valuation ratios [E6, E7], a discounted cash flow analysis reveals a 23.8% margin of safety with an intrinsic value of Rs 15,928 against the market price of Rs 12,130 [E46, E47], while the company's ROE of 27.67% and ROCE of 24.52% are more than double their respective sector benchmarks [E9, E10]. Conceded: foreign institutional holdings fell to 9.01% [E43] and institutional money flow is negative [E45], but domestic institutions have significantly increased their stake to 13.42% [E44]. Conceded: borrowings rose to Rs 22,713 Cr [E40], cash conversion was 0.25x [E34], and operating cash flow was 46% of operating profit [E37]; however, this is driven by a strategic capex build-up phase with CWIP up 2393.4% [E41] and a Rs 2,300 Cr investment to acquire 75% of KTM Austria [E87, E95]. Despite these investments, Bajaj Auto generated Rs 5,200 Cr in free cash flow over nine months [E94] and maintains a massive surplus cash position of Rs 15,000 Cr [E93]. Finally, despite metal cost pressures [E96] and absorbing the PM E-DRIVE incentive withdrawal [E97], the company achieved an all-time high Q3 EBITDA margin of 20.8% [E88] and a double-digit EBITDA margin in its scaling EV business [E90].

While the bull relies on a DCF margin of safety [E46, E47], rules-based screen signals explicitly flag decelerating earnings growth [E69] and tag trading below DCF value as a bear signal [E70], while valuation bias checks warn that a price-led five-year rally [E57] has pushed P/B to 8.73x–8.75x [E2, E7] against a sector benchmark of 2.88x [E7], meaning the price already discounts good news [E72]. The bull defends poor cash conversion of 0.25x [E34] and operating cash flow at just 46% of operating profit [E37] as strategic capex and KTM investments [E41, E87, E95], but this ignores that profits running far ahead of cash signals potential receivables or accrual risks [E34] alongside borrowings expanding dramatically to Rs 22,713 Cr [E40] and leverage reaching 0.58x debt-to-equity [E38]. Furthermore, domestic institutional buying [E44] fails to offset the overall negative institutional money flow [E45, E71] caused by foreign institutions slashing their stake by 5.36 percentage points down to 9.01% [E43]. Conceded: Q3 EBITDA margin reached 20.8% [E88] and the EV business delivers double-digit margins [E90], backed by Rs 15,000 Cr in surplus cash [E93] and nine-month free cash flow of Rs 5,200 Cr [E94]. However, cost inflation in noble and base metals has already caused a 50 basis point margin hit [E89, E96], and absorbing the loss of PM E-DRIVE incentives creates an adverse hit of INR 23,000 to INR 25,000 per electric 3-wheeler [E97], reinforcing why operating margin trends remain inconsistent on both a yearly and quarterly basis [E32, E33].

While the bear emphasizes screen flags on decelerating earnings growth [E69] and rich P/B multiples relative to the sector [E2, E7, E72], the fundamental expansion remains exceptionally strong with TTM profit growth of 55% [E21] and TTM sales growth of 37% [E17], enabling recent profit growth to outpace share price growth by 21% [E58] and earning a rules-based BUY score of 83/100 [E64] alongside a 23.8% DCF margin of safety [E47]. Conceded: cash conversion was low at 0.25x for March 2026 [E34], operating cash flow represented 46% of operating profit [E37], and borrowings increased to Rs 22,713 Cr [E40]. However, this debt reflects productive strategic investment, including over INR 2,300 Cr deployed into the Netherlands subsidiary for the KTM acquisition and BACL [E87, E95] plus a 2393.4% build-up in CWIP [E41], while core cash generation generated nearly INR 5,200 Cr in 9-month free cash flow [E94] and maintained INR 15,000 Cr in surplus cash [E93]. Furthermore, while FII stake reductions generated negative net institutional flow signals [E43, E45, E71], domestic institutions expanded their stake to 13.42% [E44] and promoters increased holdings to 55.01% [E42], supported by a strong positive sector tailwind score of +1.06 [E74, E75]. Conceded: raw material cost inflation created a 50 basis point margin drag [E89, E96] and absorbing PM E-DRIVE incentive cuts created an INR 23,000 to INR 25,000 per unit impact on electric 3-wheelers [E97]. Nevertheless, Q3 EBITDA reached a record high of over INR 3,100 Cr at a 20.8% margin [E88], the EV division continues to deliver double-digit EBITDA margins [E90], and upcoming catalysts—including 8 Pulsar product interventions over 4 months [E99] and expanding joint KTM-Triumph showrooms to over 100 [E86, E100]—position the company to outpace the expected 12% to 15% industry growth rate [E79, E80].

Conceded: Bajaj Auto delivered strong trailing TTM profit growth of 55% [E21], sales growth of 37% [E17], and carries a 23.8% DCF margin of safety [E47]. However, the bull ignores that screen flags explicitly warn of decelerating earnings growth [E69], while valuation multiples remain sharply elevated with a P/B of 8.73x against the sector's 2.88x [E2, E7, E63], an EV/EBITDA of 19.97x against 12.86x [E11], and a P/E of 29.4x [E6], confirming the bias signal that rich valuations leave no buffer as price already discounts good news [E72]. While the bull frames surging borrowings of Rs 22,713 Cr [E40] and CWIP expansion [E41] as productive alongside INR 15,000 Cr in surplus cash [E93] and 9-month free cash flow [E94], this increased debt (0.58x D/E) [E38] accompanies severely depressed cash conversion of only 0.25x [E34] and operating cash flow representing just 46% of operating profit in March 2026 [E37]. Conceded: domestic institutional holdings grew to 13.42% [E44] and promoters maintain 55.01% ownership [E42] amid sector tailwinds [E74, E75]. Yet overall institutional money flow is negative [E45, E71] as foreign institutions dumped holdings down to 9.01% [E43], taking profits in an extended stock sitting 94% up its 52-week range [E49, E73]. Furthermore, despite record Q3 EBITDA [E88] and EV profitability [E90], 3-year TTM operating margins are completely flat at 20% [E30] and inconsistent [E32, E33], dragged down by a 50 bps raw material inflation penalty [E89, E96], a INR 23,000 to INR 25,000 unit margin hit from absorbing PM E-DRIVE incentive cuts [E97], and an INR 61 Cr exceptional wage charge [E98]. Finally, execution risks surround management's Pulsar launch schedule [E99] and showroom scaling [E86, E100] to beat industry growth expectations [E79, E80], particularly as line-by-line financial consolidation of KTM Austria begins next quarter [E87, E102], exposing investors to corporate integration risks on a stock with a historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -80.7% [E54].

Bajaj Auto expects the motorcycle industry to continue growing at 12% to 15% in the near term.
evidence.quote: We expect this growth momentum in the industry to continue and the motorcycle industry to continue to grow at, say, 12% to 15%.

evidence.fact: The company expects to outpace industry growth in the 125cc plus and 150cc plus segments.
evidence.quote: Therefore, we expect to outpace industry growth in the 125cc plus segment and particularly in the 150cc plus segment and continue on the path of market share acquisition, which has commenced a couple of months ago.

evidence.fact: Bajaj Auto expects sustained growth tempo in its exports business in the coming months.
evidence.quote: Overall, the Exports business has established a sustained growth momentum, and we expect this growth tempo to continue in the coming months.

evidence.fact: Post-GST rationalization, Q3 motorcycle industry sales grew by approximately 15%.
evidence.quote: In fact, slipping to minus 3% in Q2. But post the GST rationalization, Q3 has grown by about 15% in the industry.

evidence.fact: GST cuts lifted the 3-wheeler ICE segment growth to positive 4% to 5%.
evidence.quote: The ICE segment was declining in April-August period by about 4%, but GST cuts have bumped up growth to positive 4% to 5%.

evidence.fact: The electric 3-wheeler segment continues to grow at over 50%.
evidence.quote: The Electric segment continues to drive the 3-wheeler industry by growing at about 50% plus.

evidence.fact: Chetak's retail network expanded to 450 exclusive stores and 4,000 points of sale across 800 cities and towns.
evidence.quote: The scale-up was also supported by distribution network that expanded to nearly 450 exclusive Chetak stores and 4,000 points of sale across 800 cities and towns.

evidence.fact: Bajaj Auto plans to expand joint KTM-Triumph showrooms to over 100 by March.
evidence.quote: We currently have about 50 KT showrooms operational and plan to expand these to over 100 by March.

evidence.fact: Bajaj Auto increased its ownership in KTM Austria to 75% effective November 18.
evidence.quote: Effective November 18, Bajaj ownership in KTM Austria increased to 75% and a turnaround plan was commenced immediately, which has 3 main elements to it: number one, ensure liquidity.

evidence.fact: Q3 EBITDA reached over INR 3,100 crores with an EBITDA margin of 20.8%.
evidence.quote: EBITDA came in at over INR3,100 crores at 20.8%, another all-time high and PAT crossed INR2,500 crores, yet another all-time high.

evidence.fact: Net price versus cost inflation caused a margin hit of nearly 50 basis points in Q3.
evidence.quote: As a result, we saw a net price versus cost inflation hit of nearly 50 basis points on the margin.

evidence.fact: The EV business delivers a double-digit EBITDA margin.
evidence.quote: More importantly, the EV business now delivers double-digit EBITDA margin while improving unit economics as the portfolio continues to scale.

evidence.fact: Exports volume surpassed 600,000 units in Q3 for the first time in 15 quarters.
evidence.quote: The BU crossed the 200,000 average per month sales level in October '25 after nearly 40 months and maintained this level through the remainder of the quarter, surpassing the 600,000 units mark after 15 quarters.

evidence.fact: Pro-Biking domestic volumes reached a record combined high of over 35,000 units in Q3.
evidence.quote: The 2 brands together delivered a record domestic performance with combined volumes of over 35,000 units, registering robust growth of around 50% year-on-year and marking the highest-ever quarterly performance for the business, lifted also by the positive sentiment.

evidence.fact: Bajaj Auto closed Q3 with surplus cash of approximately INR 15,000 crores.
evidence.quote: We continue to deliver strong and consistent cash generation, closing the quarter with surplus cash of about INR15,000 crores.

evidence.fact: Free cash flow generated during the first 9 months of the financial year reached nearly INR 5,200 crores.
evidence.quote: It's also worth noting that in the first 9 months of this year, we've generated nearly INR5,200 crores of free cash flow, and that was up 70% over the same period last year, reflecting our strong track record of converting profit to cash.

evidence.fact: Bajaj Auto invested over INR 2,300 crores into its Netherlands subsidiary during the 9-month period.
evidence.quote: We have strategically invested slightly above INR2,300 crores during this 9-month period into our Netherlands subsidiary, BAIHBV which you would recall was partly to fund the KTM acquisition and in the growth of BACL, which has steadily grown in scale and footprint.

evidence.fact: The company faced cost pressures across noble metals and base metals like aluminium and copper.
evidence.quote: Noble Metals especially platinum, palladium and rhodium all saw sharp increases, whilst aluminium, copper, nickel and lead also continued to harden.

evidence.fact: The withdrawal of PM E-DRIVE incentives resulted in an adverse impact of INR 23,000 to INR 25,000 per electric 3-wheeler.
evidence.quote: While the withdrawal occurred towards the later part of the quarter, the impact was meaningful at approximately INR23,000 to INR25,000 per vehicle, and we consciously chose to hold pricing and absorb this impact in order to invest behind growth and accelerate volumes and our competitive position in this segment.

evidence.fact: A one-time exceptional charge of INR 61 crores was recorded due to revised wage definitions under the new labour code.
evidence.quote: As you're all aware, pursuant to the amendment in the definition of wages under the new labour code, we recognized INR61 crores as a onetime exceptional charge towards the past service cost arising from the changes introduced under the new labour code.

evidence.fact: Management commitment: Bajaj Auto will execute 8 additional product interventions in its Pulsar portfolio over the next 4 months.
evidence.quote: The waves of these interventions will be unrelenting here onwards with over 8 more such interventions being made in the next 4 months.

evidence.fact: Management commitment: Bajaj Auto plans to expand its joint KTM-Triumph showroom count to over 100 by March.
evidence.quote: We currently have about 50 KT showrooms operational and plan to expand these to over 100 by March.

evidence.fact: Management commitment: The company expects to scale up the Riki brand footprint starting from quarter 1.
evidence.quote: We expect to start to scale up Riki beginning quarter 1.

evidence.fact: Management commitment: Starting next quarter, the KTM business will be fully consolidated line-by-line into Bajaj Auto's financial results.
evidence.quote: However, from the next quarter onwards, the KTM business will be fully consolidated into our results on a line-by-line basis as is required for subsidiaries.
